title: Saregama India Ltd - 532163 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Saregama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to Rs 263.6 crore and adjusted EBITDA 69% to Rs 112.4 crore; music vertical grew 39%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 263.6 crore (+27% YoY), adjusted EBITDA Rs 112.4 crore (+69% YoY) and operational PBT Rs 70.5 crore (+38% YoY). The music vertical (licensing, artiste management, retail) delivered Rs 230.6 crore revenue (+39%), EBITDA Rs 139.8 crore (+36%) and net margin Rs 99.6 crore (+31%). Video revenue fell 52% to about Rs 17 crore as the company winds down its films business in favour of Bhansali Productions. Management reiterated 20-23% music growth and 60-65% music EBITDA margin guidance, and asked analysts to judge performance on a rolling 12-month basis.

financial_highlights.change: +36% YoY (analyst noted music EBITDA margin down ~1% YoY on mix)
Rs 40 crore per quarter run rate over last three quarters

segments.name: Music (Licensing, Artiste Management, Retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 230.6 crore (+39% YoY), EBITDA Rs 139.8 crore (+36%), net margin Rs 99.6 crore (+31%); management attributed part of the growth to a low base in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Video
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 52% to about Rs 17 crore as films business is being wound down; remaining film releases expected to clear over the next three to four quarters.

segments.name: Artiste Management
segments.commentary: Running at about Rs 40 crore per quarter for three quarters, roughly 10% EBITDA margin per analyst; 309 artistes represented with more than 440 million followers across Instagram and YouTube.

segments.name: Live Events
segments.commentary: 23 Carvaan Live shows, 22 devotional-format shows and 48 standard packs in Q1; Ilaiyaraaja US tour underway; Arjan Dhillon tour planned for September.

segments.name: Pocket Aces (partner company)
segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 and is moving towards profitability in FY27; no revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: Bhansali Productions (partner company)
segments.commentary: No releases in Q1; next releases planned in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Music vertical revenue growth guidance maintained at 20-23% YoY on a short-to-medium-term basis.
Annual music EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 60-65%.
New music content spend for FY27 expected at Rs 300-350 crore, mostly already committed; AI-related investments to sit within this envelope.
From FY28, music content investment growth to be tempered; management aims to hold 25-30% market share.
Brand and direct-to-customer revenue split to be updated annually, not quarterly.
capex_capacity: New music content spend of Rs 300-350 crore in FY27, with large releases lined up including Love and War (January), Dharman, Paradise, Naagzilla and a Tiger Shroff Bhansali Productions film.
UN40 music festival next season set for 13-14 February 2027 in Bangalore.
Krishna show with Manoj Muntashir: 25-30 more shows planned; Carvaan Live targets a minimum of four shows per month in each city.
Diljit Dosanjh India tour tentatively planned for Q3 FY27.
Two AI teams created: one for ancillary content (podcasts, music videos), one for process optimisation; impact expected by end of calendar year.
demand_pricing: Catalog of about 180,000 songs, adding roughly 4,000-6,000 releases a year; about 60% of music revenue in FY26 came from music released after 2000, and 45% from music released after 2020.
Hit albums cited as now contributing positive margins include Stree 2, Amaran, Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani, Goat and Sarkaru Vaari Paata.

Management cites 3% paid streaming penetration in India versus 18% in Brazil and China and 57% in the US (Goldman Sachs estimates); target of 100 million paid subscribers at about Rs 100 per month, timing 12-18 months per management's personal view.
Management says catalog revenue grows at high single to low double digits on an apple-to-apple basis; new content is driving the reported mix.

Brand partnerships (Hindustan Unilever, Godrej, Lux and others) now sit in a single joint team; management did not give a revenue figure, though analysts referenced about 19% of revenue from brand tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in YouTube views and what is the outlook for brand tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specifics, attributing swings to album performance and asking for 12-month rolling review; brand selling is now a single joint team across the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why did music EBITDA margin fall about 1% YoY despite 40%+ revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix, as lower-margin Artiste Management grew faster; core licensing margins unchanged, with short-term pressure from rising content investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income decline sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was diverted to Bhansali Productions investments, reducing other income.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 and Q3 growth be strong, and what is the Artiste Management outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarterly guidance; said Artiste Management growth will temper over the next couple of quarters and margins can improve by a few percent, without quantified guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the difference in content spend between the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 cash flow statements (Rs 186 crore vs Rs 265 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not answered on the call; management said it would take the query offline.

qa_highlights.question: Subscription revenue share in licensing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share the figure, citing competition sensitivity.

risks_watch: Music EBITDA margin trajectory as content spend rises to Rs 300-350 crore; Q1 margin dipped about 1% YoY on mix.
Video segment revenue decline (-52%) during films wind-down; drag on consolidated growth over next three to four quarters.
Lumpy hit-driven revenue; the company says quarterly trends are not meaningful and asks investors to use rolling 12-month numbers.
Artiste Management growth expected to temper; margin at about 10% and new artiste onboarding is still needed to sustain growth.
Lower other income as cash is deployed into Bhansali Productions.
Unexplained content spend reconciliation between the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 cash flow presentations, pending offline response.
Paid-subscription thesis (100 million subscribers) depends on platforms curbing free content; management presented it as a personal view.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term India streaming and live-events opportunity, but evasive on quarterly guidance, subscription revenue split, AI investment quantum and advertising data, repeatedly redirecting to rolling 12-month numbers.

I feel a little wrong on our part to give guidance on a quarterly basis.
Ma'am, we don't share that specific data. It's competition sensitive data.
So, Artiste Management piece is also growing. And Artiste Management is always a lower margin. It takes zero investments.

adds.what: New music content spend of Rs 300-350 crore in FY27 (content investment, not physical capacity)
Diljit Dosanjh India tour tentatively planned (live event, not capacity)

growth.why: Management held music revenue growth guidance at 20-23% YoY (midpoint 21.5%) and music EBITDA margin at 60-65%, backed by Rs 300-350 crore FY27 content spend, though total revenue growth was 27% in Q1 and video is being wound down (down 52%) and no physical capacity additions were disclosed.
